newsitem.title: UK: Bass shares slip as outlook cautious.
newsitem.headline: Bass shares slip as outlook cautious.

text.p: Shares in brewer to hotel group Bass Plc slipped 12p to 808p in midsession trade after chairman Sir Ian Prosser adopted a cautious stance towards the group's outlook, said analysts.
Analysts also expressed concern about the possibility of slower growth on the hotels side.

"The results were pretty much in line with expectations, but it was indicated at the meeting that there was an oversupply of economy hotels where most of the group's growth is currently coming from," said Colin Davies, analyst at Goldman Sachs.
The group reported a 10 percent increase in profits before tax to 318 million stg in the six months to April 12, 1997. Brokers forecasts had ranged from 305 to 325 million.

There were also worries among analysts about delays to a government decision on the group's proposed acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley. The company first announced its plan to acquire brewer Carlsberg-Tetley in August but said it did not expect a decision on whether the deal could go ahead until mid-June.
"The company told us it is not expecting to hear before mid-June on Carlsberg-Tetley and obviously the market wants to hear as soon as possible," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"They were also perhaps not as upbeat on the outlook as on previous occassions," he added.
